text:
Alex Liu: Quick sync — proposing per-tenant sink mapping + retention tiers for trace sinks (Tempo / Honeycomb). Idea: tenants pick a retention tier (hot=30d, warm=90d, cold=365d) and we annotate spans at ingest so connectors can apply vendor-specific retention. Thoughts?
Morgan Patel: curious about cost model — do we bill per-retention tier or just by egress tokens? also how do we avoid double-storing when a span is routed to multiple vendors? :thinking_face: 
Ravi Kapoor: @Morgan good q. My thought: billing remains egress+storage; retention tier adds a multiplier on storage cost. For multi-sink we store one canonical copy, then maintain per-sink retention pointers/meta so we don't duplicate payloads.
Elaine Chen: important: Honeycomb expects dataset-level retention config and different API semantics for TTL. We need a small migrator that creates datasets and sets TTL via their API when tenant opts in. Also need key scoping if we create dataset-per-tenant.
Alex Liu: UX question — show tenant-level toggle in console + an override on each route? I prefer tenant-level default with per-route overrides for critical traces.
Morgan Patel: routing rule sketch: ```match: resource.attributes.service == "payments" and tenant.retention == "hot" -> send: tempo-us-east, honeycomb-eu (dataset=tenant-payments-hot)``` Not sure about backpressure semantics if honeycomb is slow.
Ravi Kapoor: for backpressure we should implement soft-defer + fallback: route-to-primary, monitor connector queue, if lag > X then drop non-critical sinks or switch to minimal-span subset. Also add a per-tenant retention header `x-tenant-retention:hot|warm|cold` so connectors can apply TTL on write.
Elaine Chen: watch sampling interactions — if upstream samples aggressively, we might not have enough coverage for long-retention analytics. Recommend retaining 1% of high-cardinality spans as a deterministic reservoir for cold tier.
Alex Liu: proto header example for connectors: 
```
X-Tenant-ID: t12345
X-Tenant-Retention: hot
X-Tenant-Span-Flags: keep_for=365d
```
Can connectors accept `keep_for` or should we translate into provider TTLs?
Ravi Kapoor: translate. Keep_for is a hint; connector maps to provider TTL or dataset config. Keep_for also helps internal janitor for backfill/deletes.
tempo-bot: connector-honeycomb: created dataset tenant-t12345-payments-hot (ttl=30d)
Morgan Patel: console idea: show a retention heatmap per-tenant (active spans/day) + cost estimate change when you flip tiers. small CTA to preview dataset changes.
Elaine Chen: + audit log entry when retention changes and when dataset created/modified. This is a compliance must.
Alex Liu: ok next steps: 1) RFC for header + connector mapping 2) small migrator prototype for honeycomb datasets 3) console mock for tenant retention toggle. I'll post RFC link tomorrow. Thanks all :thumbsup:
